A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PaAno research work. All 28 pages, including Appendices A–E, equations, figures, and tables, are available and readable enough for reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original PaAno benchmark results, runtime measurements, and ablation and sensitivity experiments in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V2 reports revised original PaAno benchmark results, runtime measurements, and ablation and sensitivity experiments in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the patch encoder, triplet/pretext objectives, farthest-negative selection, coreset memory bank, and anomaly-scoring procedure. Revised hyperparameters and newly disclosed loss scaling do not establish a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate univariate and multivariate anomaly detection on TSB-AD-U and TSB-AD-M. Table 15 retains the same constituent subsets and represented data; no new task or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: The full benchmark tables retain the same comparator sets. However, Figure 8’s top-12 multivariate score-distribution comparison replaces AutoEncoder, KMeansAD, and CBLOF with iTransformer, NLinear, and PatchTST.

E3.justification: The reported training budget drops from 200 to 100 iterations, the triplet margin changes from 0.5 to 0.1, and the univariate patch size changes from 64 to 96. Tables 2–3 also substantially revise reported baseline capacities: PatchTST changes from 0.5M to 6.9M parameters, and iTransformer from 0.6M to 6.3M/6.4M. These materially revise the stated experimental configurations, without establishing which baseline revisions reflect reruns or reporting corrections.

E4.justification: The existing ablation and sensitivity program is retained. Table 9 replaces the initial 10% pretext-loss duration with 20% under the shorter training budget, and Figure 8 revises the selected distribution comparisons. No new robustness scenario or substantially different analytical question is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten repetitions with different random seeds and report averages. Table 15 retains the same plus/minus uncertainty-reporting practice; changed uncertainty values do not constitute a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Benchmark, subset, and ablation values and rankings change extensively. Table 15’s PaAno VUS-PR changes from 0.5188 to 0.5296 on TSB-AD-U and from 0.4307 to 0.4263 on TSB-AD-M. In Table 2, KAN-AD changes from 0.43 to 0.40, making (Sub)-PCA’s 0.42 the best baseline score. Table 8’s univariate median-negative result changes from 45.5% to 52.8%. Reported runtimes also decrease. These are revised results accompanying changed settings, not controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The formal method equations, normal-training-data assumption, and Appendix C metric definitions are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: lightweight patch-based representation learning, strong univariate and multivariate detection, computational efficiency, and hyperparameter robustness.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 replaces the interpretation that median negatives provide weak contrast with an acknowledgment that explicitly selected median and closest negatives offer useful learning signals. Appendix D.1 revises the encoder interpretation, including replacing OmniCNN’s reported univariate advantage with evidence favoring the default 1D-CNN. These are substantive but localized explanatory revisions.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly discloses dividing the triplet loss by ten and updates documented defaults. The encoder-layer description, baseline search grids, hardware information, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to prior anomaly-detection and representation-learning methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized paragraphs in Section 4.2 and Appendices D–E are rewritten to match revised findings, with small wording corrections and paragraph reflow. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 lose their grouped column headers, several tables reorder rows, and figures are updated or redrawn within the existing presentation structure. Figure 8 changes its selected boxes. Figures 6–7 relabel their vertical axes from 'Average Run Time' to 'Average Inference Time,' while their captions still say runtime.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful loss-scaling information and fixes cross-table inconsistencies: DADA’s Point-F1 in Table 2 now matches Table 16, and Table 4’s scheduling ablations agree with Table 9. However, Figures 6–7 newly label timing as inference while Appendix E.3 still includes training, creating ambiguity in the central efficiency evidence. Updated scores under changed settings do not independently establish better paper quality. These benefits and reporting problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
